items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new `punycode(domain)` helper is clearly named and has a docstring. It replaces the inline idna try/except in `sanitize_address` with a single readable line, and the formatting matches the surrounding Django code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: There is one shared helper, and it is applied at the source in `get_fqdn`. But `make_msgid(domain=punycode(str(DNS_NAME)))` converts the name a second time. That redundant call exists only so the issue's test, which patches in a plain string, passes.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed and no try/except hides failures. `punycode` leaves ASCII names unchanged and is safe to apply twice. It has the same failure behaviour on invalid labels as the reference.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: `self._fqdn = punycode(socket.getfqdn())` converts the name at the source, so it works for every encoding. ASCII hostnames come through unchanged. Converting an already-ASCII name again at `make_msgid` does nothing, so there is no double-encoding. The hidden tests pass.
